editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout: the "will not be charged unless" caveat ("Tu ne seras pas facturé à moins de créer une instance du plan Pay-As-You-Go…"), the underlined cost warning ("entraîneront un coût") and the "or other free plan, if you have one" qualifier all survive, and the informal "tu" register holds consistently.

Entry [223] is the sentence that defines the Toffoli gate, and it renders "controlled-controlled-NOT" as "opération NOT-NOT contrôlée-contrôlée". Doubling NOT tells the learner the gate applies NOT twice, when it is one NOT with two controls. In [178], "the *reverse*, or in mathematical terms the *inverse*" becomes "l'*inverse*, ou en termes mathématiques l'*inverse*", which says the same word twice and loses the point being made about the two terms. Smaller problems: the French mixes "controlled-U"/"controlled-X" and "opération *swap*" ([206], [213], [215]) with "NOT contrôlé", "opérations unitaires contrôlées" and "opération d'échange"; [77] is a calque ("équivalent à |ψ⟩ étant un vecteur unitaire"); and [8] has a grammar error ("pour tout états"). The rest is faithful and reads naturally, for example "état produit", "intriqués", "base de Bell" and "mesures partielles".

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. examples.source: Classical repetition codes
examples.translation: Codes répétitifs classiques
examples.suggested: Codes de répétition classiques

examples.translation: l'espace des vecteurs propres $-1$ pour cet observable

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the bounds in the last part: the 4/π² bound (above 40%) and the 1/4 bound (at most 25%) are kept, as are the "at most 25% of the time" majority-vote argument and the claim that errors fall off exponentially. In [233], "la probabilité peu probable" is redundant. "Facteur préfixe" in [99] and "un coût de calcul significatif est engagé" in [180] read like translationese. examples.translation: un coût de calcul significatif est engagé à mesure que m augmente

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the late sections on the number field sieve, NP-completeness, the exponential-time hypothesis and uniformity. Nothing here would mislead a learner. A French technical editor would still fix a few calques and one misplaced adjective. The heading "Ensembles de portes universelles" makes the gates universal when it is the set that is universal. "assez moins convaincants" [121] is not idiomatic French. "seulement pratique pour" [97] is calqued from English. The number field sieve is called "crible algébrique des corps de nombres" [109, 115, 118], a redundant mix of two standard names. The negated conjecture in [117] is clumsy, and "avec haute probabilité" [111] should be "avec une forte probabilité".

examples.translation: Ensembles de portes universelles

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. examples.suggested: simplifier l'équivalence de la promesse, qui s'écrit alors

examples.source: a promise problem with a flavor similar to the Deutsch-Jozsa and Bernstein-Vazirani problems
examples.translation: un problème avec promesse, dont la saveur est similaire aux problèmes de Deutsch-Jozsa
examples.suggested: un problème avec promesse, dans le même esprit que les problèmes de Deutsch-Jozsa et de Bernstein-Vazirani
examples.why: 'Saveur' is a literal calque of the figurative 'flavor'.

examples.source: by taking the bits of these strings as binary-valued entries
examples.translation: en prenant les bits de ces chaînes comme entrées binaires
examples.suggested: en prenant les bits de ces chaînes comme coefficients binaires

examples.source: each execution of the circuit provides us with statistical evidence concerning $s$
examples.translation: chaque exécution du circuit nous fournit une preuve statistique concernant $s$
examples.suggested: chaque exécution du circuit nous fournit une information statistique sur $s$

editor_note: The translation is faithful and should not mislead a learner. Core terms are correct and used consistently: matrice densité, état complètement mélangé, semi-définie positive, théorème spectral, base orthonormée. A native editor would still change three things. In [69], the comma has moved inside the math span ("Autrement dit$,A$"), so the page renders a stray ",A". In [56], the matrix entries are called "entrées hors-diagonale", a calque; "coefficients hors diagonale" or "non diagonaux" is the usual French. In [76], "there will be different ways" has been softened to "il peut exister différentes façons". That wording is defensible, but it is weaker than the English.

examples.source: That is, we may have that $A$ is $n\times m$
examples.translation: Autrement dit$,A$ peut être de taille $n\times m$
examples.suggested: Autrement dit, $A$ peut être de taille $n\times m$
examples.why: The comma has been pulled inside the math delimiters, so the page renders a stray ',A' in math font and the space after 'dit' is gone.

examples.source: off-diagonal entries describe the degree to which ...
examples.translation: les entrées hors-diagonale décrivent le degré de superposition quantique
examples.suggested: les coefficients hors diagonale (non diagonaux) décrivent ...
examples.why: 'entrées' for matrix entries is a calque of English, and 'hors-diagonale' is not the usual form. French linear algebra says 'coefficients non diagonaux' or 'hors diagonale'.

examples.source: it must be understood that there will be different ways to write a density matrix
examples.translation: il faut comprendre qu'il peut exister différentes façons d'écrire
examples.suggested: il faut bien comprendre qu'il existe en général différentes façons d'écrire
examples.why: The English makes a firm statement ('there will be'), and 'il peut exister' turns it into a possibility. This is minor because pure states are an exception anyway, but the emphasis of the lesson is weaker.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the Kraus/Choi equivalence proofs, the partial-measurement section and the p(a)=0 caveat in [140], and the core terms are consistent (matrice densité, semi-définie positive, canal de déphasage complet, état classique-quantique). A native editor would still fix a few things. Matrix entries are calqued as "entrées" ("entrées hors-diagonale", "entrées diagonales") where French uses "coefficients". "on définit effectivement" in [124] is a false friend for "in effect". "les probabilités somment à 1" is anglicized. In [47] "De plus$,P_0 + P_1 = \mathbb{I}$" moves the comma inside the math and drops the space, so it renders as "De plus,P0+P1=I".

examples.source: it zeros out all of the off-diagonal entries of an input matrix
examples.translation: il annule toutes les entrées hors-diagonale d'une matrice d'entrée
examples.suggested: il annule tous les coefficients hors diagonale d'une matrice d'entrée
examples.why: 'entrées' for matrix entries is an anglicism. French linear algebra says 'coefficients'. The same calque appears in [77], [87] and [94].

examples.source: we're effectively defining a measurement of (X,Z)
examples.translation: on définit effectivement une mesure de $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Z})$
examples.suggested: on définit en fait une mesure de $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Z})$
examples.why: 'effectivement' means 'indeed' in French, not 'in effect'. It is a false friend.

examples.source: ensures that the probabilities sum to $1$
examples.translation: garantit que les probabilités somment à $1$
examples.suggested: garantit que la somme des probabilités vaut $1$
examples.why: 'sommer à' is a calque of 'sum to'.

examples.source: We also have that $P_0 + P_1 = \mathbb{I}$
examples.translation: De plus$,P_0 + P_1 = \mathbb{I}$
examples.suggested: De plus, $P_0 + P_1 = \mathbb{I}$
examples.why: The comma is moved inside the math delimiter and the space is lost, so the text renders glued together. The qualifier 'happen to be' is also dropped from the eigenvalue sentence.

examples.source: we're just using these names to keep things simple
examples.translation: nous utilisons ces noms simplement pour rester concis
examples.suggested: nous utilisons ces noms simplement pour ne pas compliquer les choses
examples.why: 'keep things simple' is about simplicity, not brevity. This is a small shift that does not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The existence proof, the Schmidt decomposition, the unitary equivalence proof, bit commitment and Hughston-Jozsa-Wootters all match the English, and the informal "tu" is kept (Considère, Suppose, Note). A French math editor would still change a few things. "uniquely determined" is calqued as "uniquement déterminés" in entries [45], [47], [61], [63], [86] and [87], where French expects "déterminés de manière unique"; "entier positif" should be "entier strictement positif"; "ce qui complète la preuve" and "il pourrait être que N = …" are anglicisms. In [110], "dans quel état de Bell il se trouve" wrongly suggests that Bob himself is in a Bell state, and in [102] and [129] a comma has slipped inside the math delimiters ("expressions$,r$", "arbitraire$,(p_0").

examples.source: which are uniquely determined (up to their ordering)
examples.translation: qui sont uniquement déterminés (à leur ordre près)
examples.suggested: qui sont déterminés de manière unique (à l'ordre près)
examples.why: 'uniquement déterminés' is a calque that literally reads 'only determined'. The standard French idiom is 'déterminés de manière unique'. The same calque recurs in entries 47, 61, 63, 86 and 87.

examples.source: for any positive integer $n$
examples.translation: pour tout entier positif $n$
examples.suggested: pour tout entier strictement positif $n$
examples.why: In French, 'positif' includes zero, so n = 0 would be allowed. The English means n ≥ 1. The same applies to 'entier positif arbitraire' in entry 129.

examples.source: to see which Bell state he holds
examples.translation: pour savoir dans quel état de Bell il se trouve
examples.suggested: pour déterminer quel état de Bell il détient
examples.why: 'il se trouve' can be read as Bob himself being in a Bell state. The English means the state of the pair of qubits he holds.

examples.source: which completes the proof.
examples.translation: ce qui complète la preuve.
examples.suggested: ce qui achève la démonstration.
examples.why: This is an English calque. French mathematical prose uses 'achève/conclut la démonstration'.

examples.source: it could be that $N = 1,000,000$ while X and Y are qubits
examples.translation: il pourrait être que $N = 1\,000\,000$ tandis que ...
examples.suggested: on pourrait avoir $N = 1\,000\,000$ alors que ...
examples.why: 'il pourrait être que' is a literal rendering of 'it could be that' and is not idiomatic French.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout: the cycle of implications, the conditions on the Choi and Kraus representations, and the block construction of U are all rendered faithfully, so nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix a few things. [36] has a gender agreement error ("les valeurs propres … ils ont") and the awkward "on en a une telle expression". [81] copies English syntax in "équivalent à $N$ étant un multiple". [122] renders "Tracing out a system" as "Tracer un système", where "tracer" reads as "to draw". [104] uses the anglicism "produit interne" where French usually says "produit scalaire", and [85] has the stiff "termes plus formulaires".

examples.source: because the eigenvalues are nonnegative real numbers, they have nonnegative square roots
examples.translation: comme les valeurs propres sont des réels non négatifs, ils ont des racines carrées non négatives
examples.suggested: comme les valeurs propres sont des réels non négatifs, elles ont des racines carrées non négatives
examples.why: Gender agreement error: 'valeurs propres' is feminine. The same entry also has the clumsy 'on en a une telle expression' (better: 'on dispose d'une telle expression').

examples.source: which is equivalent to $N$ being a multiple of $n/\operatorname{gcd}(n,m)$
examples.translation: ce qui est équivalent à $N$ étant un multiple de $n/\operatorname{gcd}(n,m)$
examples.suggested: ce qui revient à dire que $N$ est un multiple de $n/\operatorname{gcd}(n,m)$
examples.why: The gerund construction copies English syntax and is ungrammatical in French.

examples.source: Tracing out a system.
examples.translation: Tracer un système.
examples.suggested: Prendre la trace partielle sur un système.
examples.why: 'Tracer' in French means to draw or plot. The operation meant here is a partial trace.

examples.source: compute the inner product between any two of these vectors
examples.translation: Calculons maintenant le produit interne entre deux quelconques de ces vecteurs
examples.suggested: Calculons maintenant le produit scalaire de deux quelconques de ces vecteurs
examples.why: 'Produit scalaire' is the standard French term. 'Produit interne' is an anglicism, though still recognizable.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The claims about limits and caveats in [30]-[36] and [62] come through intact, and the tu register holds. A native editor would still fix some English-shaped phrasing: "L'IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit" [15] leaves an English compound in the sentence, "prendrait des ordres de grandeur de plus que l'âge" [31] is ungrammatical, and "espaces de recherche extrêmement larges" [36] and "ne peuvent pas compléter" [32] copy English word choices. "Quantum-centric supercomputing" is rendered as "supercalcul quantique centré" [39], which is wrong in French and repeats "déjà". In [43] "scale-up" is dropped from the second tier. The link titles in [21] and [59] were changed without the source changing: [21] was corrected to match its URL, and in [59] "Run your first circuit on hardware" became "Hello world".

examples.source: The IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit was the first HPC resource to achieve ExaOPS
examples.translation: L'IBM-built Oak Ridge Summit fut la première ressource HPC à atteindre les ExaOPS
examples.suggested: Le supercalculateur Summit d'Oak Ridge, construit par IBM, fut la première ressource HPC à atteindre l'ExaOPS
examples.why: An English compound adjective is left in the middle of the French sentence.

examples.source: the calculation would take orders of magnitude longer than the current age of our Sun
examples.translation: le calcul prendrait des ordres de grandeur de plus que l'âge actuel de notre Soleil
examples.suggested: le calcul prendrait des ordres de grandeur plus longtemps que l'âge actuel de notre Soleil
examples.why: "prendre des ordres de grandeur de plus que" is ungrammatical. The comparison needs "plus longtemps".

examples.source: quantum‑centric supercomputing (QCSC) reference architecture ... which already show accuracy
examples.translation: architecture de référence pour le supercalcul quantique centré (QCSC) ... qui ont déjà fait leurs preuves ... qui montrent déjà
examples.suggested: architecture de référence pour le supercalcul centré sur le quantique (QCSC) ... des flux de travail hybrides éprouvés ... qui atteignent déjà
examples.why: "supercalcul quantique centré" misparses "quantum-centric". The sentence also stacks two relative clauses and says "déjà" twice.

examples.source: Co‑located CPU/GPU scale‑up systems connected via near‑time interconnects
examples.translation: Systèmes CPU/GPU co-localisés connectés via des interconnexions à quasi-temps réel
examples.suggested: Systèmes CPU/GPU co-localisés à montée en charge verticale (scale-up), reliés par des interconnexions quasi temps réel
examples.why: "scale-up" is dropped. That word is what separates this tier from the scale-out tier that follows.

examples.source: problems with extremely large search spaces
examples.translation: des problèmes avec des espaces de recherche extrêmement larges
examples.suggested: des problèmes dont les espaces de recherche sont extrêmement vastes
examples.why: "larges" copies the English "large". French uses "vastes" or "immenses" for the size of a space.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing would mislead a learner. The superposition, measurement collapse, probability and entanglement passages all match the source, and the core terms stay consistent: intrication, superposition, portes quantiques, calcul quantique. A native editor would still fix a few things. The coin labels swap the French convention: heads is 'face', not 'pile'. There are also several calques: 'modifier le mot' (should be 'qualifier'), 'étudiant diplômé' for graduate student, 'la marque de 06:17 minutes' and 'haute probabilité'. Two smaller points: 'intractable' is rendered as 'insurmontables', and 'almost transparent' lost its qualifier in the scarf metaphor.

examples.source: two possible sides which we will call "heads" (H) and "tails" (T)
examples.translation: que nous appellerons « pile » (P) et « face » (F), respectivement
examples.suggested: que nous appellerons « face » (F) et « pile » (P), respectivement (and the lists in [41]-[43] reordered to match)
examples.why: In French, heads is 'face' and tails is 'pile'. With 'respectivement', the sentence maps them the wrong way round. It doesn't break the counting, but it is wrong.

examples.source: The words “classical” and “quantum” came to modify the word “computing”
examples.translation: Les mots « classique » et « quantique » sont venus modifier le mot « informatique »
examples.suggested: sont venus qualifier le mot « informatique »
examples.why: In the grammatical sense, 'modify' is 'qualifier' in French. 'Modifier' reads as though the word itself was changed.

examples.source: to a child, teen, college student, graduate student ... Please watch up to the 06:17-minute mark
examples.translation: un étudiant universitaire, un étudiant diplômé ... Regarde jusqu'à la marque de 06:17 minutes
examples.suggested: un étudiant de licence, un doctorant ... Regarde au moins jusqu'à 6 min 17
examples.why: 'Étudiant diplômé' is a calque of 'graduate student', and 'la marque de ... minutes' is translationese.

examples.source: There are still intractable computational problems
examples.translation: des problèmes computationnels insurmontables
examples.suggested: des problèmes de calcul insolubles en pratique (intraitables)
examples.why: 'Intractable' has a technical meaning (too costly to compute), and 'insurmontables' loses it. 'Problèmes de calcul' also reads more naturally than 'computationnels'.

examples.source: very thin, sheer scarves that are almost transparent
examples.translation: deux écharpes très fines et transparentes
examples.suggested: deux écharpes très fines, presque transparentes
examples.why: The 'almost' qualifier was dropped. It is minor, but the metaphor relies on seeing both colors combine.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the resilience levels, ZNE/PEA/PEC and the transpiler stages, so nothing would mislead a learner. The worst slip is in [26], where "job" became "emploi" (a job as in employment); it should be "tâche" or "job". Several terms are rendered inconsistently: "transpileur" in [41]/[54] but "transpilateur" everywhere else. Pauli twirling appears as "tourbillonnement de Pauli" in [69]/[79] but "Pauli twirling" in [71]. The Map step is "Mapper" in [40] but "Correspondance" in [44]/[45]. Sampler/Estimator are lowercase in [26] but capitalized "l'Échantillonneur/l'Estimateur" in [73]. There are also smaller slips: the "flag" calque in [56], the typo "décoherence" in [36], "inducteur" in [11] where French uses "inductance", and "fil de soudure / coule" in [13].

examples.source: design a larger circuit or job
examples.translation: concevoir un circuit ou un emploi plus grand
examples.suggested: concevoir un circuit ou une tâche (job) plus grande
examples.why: 'emploi' means employment. It is a wrong-sense word for a computing job and leaves the reader puzzled.

examples.source: using the Qiskit transpiler
examples.translation: en utilisant le transpilateur Qiskit
examples.suggested: Pick one form (transpileur) and use it everywhere
examples.why: [41] and [54] use 'transpileur' but [55]-[78] use 'transpilateur', so the same tool has two names in one file.

examples.source: dynamical decoupling and Pauli twirling
examples.translation: le découplage dynamique et le tourbillonnement de Pauli
examples.suggested: le découplage dynamique et le Pauli twirling
examples.why: [71] keeps 'Pauli twirling', while [69] and [79] use the invented calque 'tourbillonnement'. The rendering is inconsistent and not the usual French term.

examples.source: There is an argument you can flag in the transpiler
examples.translation: Il y a un argument que tu peux signaler dans le transpilateur
examples.suggested: Il existe une option que tu peux activer dans le transpileur
examples.why: 'signaler' is a literal calque of 'flag'. Here it means enabling an option.

examples.source: due to the decoherence times of the qubits
examples.translation: en raison des temps de décoherence des qubits
examples.suggested: en raison des temps de décohérence des qubits
examples.why: Spelling error: the French term is 'décohérence'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The cut counts, the four max-cut solutions, the fifth-most-probable caveat and the list of error sources all match the English. In [101] and [102], "plot" (the histogram) is rendered as "graphe". On a page about graph theory that word already means the max-cut graph, so "graphique"/"histogramme" would be clearer. A few terms are also rendered inconsistently: "Estimator/Sampler" becomes "l'estimateur ou du sampler", "transpiler" is kept as a French noun instead of "transpileur", and the article switches between "l'Hamiltonien" and "le Hamiltonien". There are also some calques, such as "nous salir les mains" and "à deux corps locaux".

examples.source: (Remember – the order of the qubits is reversed in the plot bitstrings!)
examples.translation: (Souviens-toi — l'ordre des qubits est inversé dans les chaînes de bits du graphe !)
examples.suggested: (Souviens-toi — l'ordre des qubits est inversé dans les chaînes de bits de l'histogramme !)
examples.why: On a max-cut page "graphe" means the graph being partitioned. Using it for the plot is ambiguous: it suggests the reversal applies to the graph itself.

examples.source: From this plot, we can take the most likely bitstring and represent it as a partitioned graph
examples.translation: À partir de ce graphe, nous pouvons prendre la chaîne de bits la plus probable et la représenter comme un graphe partitionné
examples.suggested: À partir de cet histogramme, nous pouvons prendre la chaîne de bits la plus probable et la représenter comme un graphe partitionné
examples.why: "graphe" is used twice in one sentence with two different meanings (plot vs. graph).

examples.source: A single primitive request of the Estimator or Sampler primitive
examples.translation: Une seule requête primitive de l'estimateur ou du sampler
examples.suggested: Une seule requête de la primitive Estimator ou Sampler
examples.why: One Qiskit primitive name is translated and the other isn't. Both are API names and should stay as Estimator/Sampler.

examples.source: since the transpiler optimizes differently for different processors
examples.translation: car le transpiler optimise différemment selon les processeurs
examples.suggested: car le transpileur optimise différemment selon les processeurs
examples.why: "transpiler" is a French verb. The conventional French noun is "transpileur".

examples.source: we'll get our hands dirty with a utility-scale example
examples.translation: nous allons nous salir les mains avec un exemple
examples.suggested: nous allons mettre les mains dans le cambouis avec un exemple
examples.why: Literal calque of the English idiom. In French, "se salir les mains" suggests doing something morally dubious.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the configuration-recovery walkthrough, the flip-probability tables and the chemical-accuracy caveat. Nothing here would mislead a learner. Some polish is still needed. "Eigensolver" is rendered as "solveur propre" in [62] and [95] but as "solveur d'états propres" in [85] and [93]. Entry [78] leaves "occupancies" in English and slips into vous ("Notez que") right after "noter que". A few calques read stiffly: "ce qui résulte en moins de portes" [55], "ce qui manque des vecteurs du support" [98] and "$N_x$ nombres de $1$s" [67].

examples.source: is then fed into an Eigensolver
examples.translation: est ensuite transmis à un solveur propre (Eigensolver)
examples.suggested: est ensuite transmis à un solveur de valeurs propres (eigensolver)
examples.why: "Solveur propre" is not a French term, and the file also uses "solveur d'états propres" in [85]/[93]. Pick one rendering and use it everywhere.

examples.source: (in short _occupancies_) ... Note that, as per Qiskit ordering convention
examples.translation: (en abrégé _occupancies_) ... Notez que, selon la convention d'ordre de Qiskit
examples.suggested: (en abrégé _occupations_) ... Note que, selon la convention d'ordre de Qiskit
examples.why: The English term is left untranslated even though the tables use "Occupation", and "Notez" breaks the tu register.

examples.source: which is missing vectors from ground state support
examples.translation: ce qui manque des vecteurs du support de l'état fondamental
examples.suggested: auquel il manque des vecteurs du support de l'état fondamental
examples.why: This is a calque of "is missing" and is ungrammatical in French.

examples.source: resulting in fewer gates in the final circuit
examples.translation: ce qui résulte en moins de portes dans le circuit final
examples.suggested: ce qui réduit le nombre de portes du circuit final
examples.why: "Résulter en" is an anglicism.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. I found no inverted negations, swapped quantities or dropped caveats, and the "tu" register holds everywhere. There are several calques to fix. "quantum mechanical processes" becomes "processus quantiques mécaniques" [29]. "computationally intractable" becomes "insolubles computationnellement" [41], which is slightly stronger than the English; the standard term is "intraitables". Other anglicisms are "sont mieux compris comme" [25], "retourner les meilleurs résultats" and "nous prédisons" [22], and "mapping" [51, 60]. "Hamiltonien(s)" is capitalized [29, 51], while the adjective "hamiltonienne" is lowercase; French convention lowercases the noun too. "hype" switches between « hype » and "du hype" [4].

examples.source: simulating quantum mechanical processes found in nature
examples.translation: la simulation de processus quantiques mécaniques trouvés dans la nature
examples.suggested: la simulation des processus de mécanique quantique présents dans la nature
examples.why: This is a word-by-word calque; 'quantiques mécaniques' is not idiomatic French.

examples.source: often become computationally intractable as the problem size grows
examples.translation: deviennent souvent insolubles computationnellement
examples.suggested: deviennent souvent intraitables en pratique (d'un point de vue calculatoire)
examples.why: 'Insoluble' means 'has no solution', which is stronger than 'intractable'. The standard complexity term is 'intraitable'.

examples.source: Instead, we predict both will be used together to return the best possible results from quantum computers.
examples.translation: À la place, nous prédisons que les deux seront utilisées ensemble pour retourner les meilleurs résultats possibles
examples.suggested: Nous prévoyons plutôt que les deux seront utilisées conjointement pour obtenir les meilleurs résultats possibles
examples.why: 'prédire' and 'retourner' are calques of 'predict' and 'return'.

examples.source: today's quantum computers are best understood as hybrid systems
examples.translation: les ordinateurs quantiques d'aujourd'hui sont mieux compris comme des systèmes hybrides
examples.suggested: il est plus juste de voir les ordinateurs quantiques actuels comme des systèmes hybrides
examples.why: This keeps the English passive construction, which reads stiffly in French.

examples.source: the natural mapping between optimization objectives and quantum Hamiltonians
examples.translation: du mapping naturel entre les objectifs d'optimisation et les Hamiltoniens quantiques
examples.suggested: de la correspondance naturelle entre les objectifs d'optimisation et les hamiltoniens quantiques
examples.why: 'mapping' is an unnecessary anglicism. 'Hamiltoniens' is capitalized, unlike the adjective 'hamiltonienne' elsewhere in the file.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. Local versus global trade-offs, bootstrapping ("amorçage"), gradient-free methods and barren plateaus ("plateaux stériles") are rendered accurately and consistently, and the tu register holds in the summary. Two stylistic slips remain. In [31], the parenthetical "(et donc de plus en plus difficile pour déterminer la direction…)" is ungrammatical in French. In [8], "À haut niveau" is a calque of "At a high level".

examples.source: (and thus more challenging to determine the direction to the minimum)
examples.translation: (et donc de plus en plus difficile pour déterminer la direction vers le minimum)
examples.suggested: (ce qui rend de plus en plus difficile la détermination de la direction du minimum)
examples.why: The clause has no subject, and 'difficile pour déterminer' is a calque. French needs 'difficile de déterminer' or a nominal construction.

examples.source: At a high level, optimizers are central to exploring our search space.
examples.translation: À haut niveau, les optimiseurs sont au cœur de l'exploration de notre espace de recherche.
examples.suggested: Dans les grandes lignes, les optimiseurs sont au cœur de l'exploration de notre espace de recherche.
examples.why: 'À haut niveau' is a literal calque. A native writer would say 'Dans les grandes lignes' or 'De manière générale'.
